messages:
jon: thinking out loud: pilot a 'progressive acceptance' onboarding where we combine tiny golden checks + synthetic stress tests + runtime compatibility matrix. goal: catch correctness + perf + footprint issues earlier while keeping cost bounded.

mei: sounds good. can you outline concrete phases?

jon: phase A: lint & tokenizer hash + binary size/format checks. phase B: targeted golden by seqlen buckets (5 inputs per bucket). phase C: synthetic stress (burst qps, long prefixes, kv heavy) on a dev GPU pool. phase D: runtime compatibility sweep across the three runtimes (hosted/dedicated/private) with smoke traffic. phase E: opt-in shadow on low qps prod.

raf: question: how many seqlen buckets? do we pick [16,64,256,1024]?

jon: propose these 4 buckets. objective is to catch pathological latencies and memory blowups. each bucket has representative prompts with common tokens + edge-case tokens (emoji, CJK).

nora: we should also add an abi check for serialized weights (float16 vs int8 metadata) so runtime can reject early. earlier we had a mismatch where quant metadata was absent.

sam: cost model: if we run 5 golden per bucket that's 20 in total. synthetic stress is the heavy part; propose we run synthetic for 30s at 2x expected qps on a cheap instance to surface tail lat issues.

mei: for synthetic stress we should randomize prefixes and KV accesses. can we reuse perf-fuzz harness?

raf: yes reuse perf-fuzz but add a small adapter to tag requests by bucket and record kv-shape metrics.

jon: acceptance criteria idea: hard blocks = tokenizer mismatch, hash mismatch, out-of-memory on any bucket, model ABI missing quant metadata. soft blocks = avg p95 > baseline*2 or token failure rate > 1%. informational = <2x p95 but still statistically different.

nora: about compatibility sweep: do we require a full run on private infra? that could be expensive for pilot.

jon: for pilot run a lightweight runtime probe: verify model loads, a short infer (10 samples) and kv sanity. Full private run reserved for models tagged enterprise.

sam: telemetry: we need these metrics emitted from runners: bucket_p95_ms, bucket_mem_peak_mb, kv_shape_mismatch, token_err_rate, synth_tail_ratio. also emit sample outputs for golden diffs.

mei: for diffs, can we surface granular deltas: top tokens that changed across runs + a normalized divergence score? that helps prioritize regressions.

raf: agree. add "top_tokens_delta" and "divergence_score" to golden report.

jon: config sketch (mini-schema):
```
stages: ["lint","targeted_golden","synth_stress","runtime_probe","shadow" ]
buckets: [16,64,256,1024]
golden_per_bucket: 5
synth: {"duration_s": 30, "qps_mult": 2}
acceptance: {"hard_blocks": ["tokenizer_hash","oom","abi_missing"], "soft_block_thresholds": {"p95_mult": 2.0, "token_err_rate": 0.01}}
```

jon: this is intentionally compact so infra can map steps to jobs.

nora: security/privacy: golden inputs must be scrubbed and labeled as "test_only" and stored in KMS bucket. also access limited.

sam: ops-bot: can you automate a per-model ephemeral test workspace with IAM-limited creds?

ops-bot: workspace-create: temporary test workspace created for model-id=mdl_2026_07_12, expires in 7d.

mei: ownership: raf will adapt perf-fuzz, nora will own lint/abi checks, jon will spec the golden sets and config. sam will wire telemetry and cost guardrails. i'll draft the short RFC.

raf: timeline: aim for an initial pilot in 10 working days. can we scope a single open model to start?

jon: yes pick an LlamaX open variant. keep it cheap.

nora: one more: add a rollback invariant: any hard block must prevent model from being promoted to shadow; soft blocks require ops review before rollout.

sam: noted. I'll add an alerting playbook: if synth_tail_ratio > 1.5x baseline or token_err_rate spikes, auto-disable shadow and notify #eng-oncall.

jon: thanks all. i'll post a tiny RFC and attach the golden candidate list. any objections?

mei: none. excited to see synth stress uncover weird edgecases. :rocket:

raf: ack.

nora: ack.

ops-bot: scheduled: perf-fuzz job queued for 1744222400.
